- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

21		case "mysql":

23		case "postgres":

27		}

29			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to create db driver")
30		}
31		return driver, nil

21	// NewDB opens a database specified by its database driver name and a
22	// driver-specific data source name, usually consisting of at least a

24	func NewDB(profile *profile.Profile) (store.Driver, error) {
25		// Ensure a DSN is set before attempting to open the database.
26		if profile.DSN == "" {
27			return nil, errors.New("dsn required")

36		}

39		// - No shared-cache: it's obsolete; WAL journal mode is a better solution.
40		// - No foreign key constraints: it's currently disabled by default, but it's a
41		// good practice to be explicit and prevent future surprises on SQLite upgrades.
42		// - Journal mode set to WAL: it's the recommended journal mode for most applications
43		// as it prevents locking issues.
44		// - mmap size set to 0: it disables memory mapping, which can cause OOM errors on some systems.
45		//
46		// Notes:
47		// - When using the `modernc.org/sqlite` driver, each pragma must be prefixed with `_pragma=`.
48		//
49		// References:
50		// - https://pkg.go.dev/modernc.org/sqlite#Driver.Open
51		// - https://www.sqlite.org/sharedcache.html
52		// - https://www.sqlite.org/pragma.html
53		sqliteDB, err := sql.Open("sqlite", profile.DSN+"?_pragma=foreign_keys(0)&_pragma=busy_timeout(10000)&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)&_pragma=mmap_size(0)")
54		if err != nil {
55			return nil, errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to open db with dsn: %s", profile.DSN)
56		}
57	
58		driver := DB{db: sqliteDB, profile: profile}
59	
60		return &driver, nil
61	}
62	
63	func (d *DB) GetDB() *sql.DB {
64		return d.db
65	}
66	
67	func (d *DB) Close() error {
68		return d.db.Close()
69	}
70	
71	func (d *DB) IsInitialized(ctx context.Context) (bool, error) {
72		// Check if the database is initialized by checking if the memo table exists.
73		var exists bool
74		err := d.db.QueryRowContext(ctx, "SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='memo')").Scan(&exists)
75		if err != nil {
76			return false, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to check if database is initialized")
77		}
78		return exists, nil
79	}
80	
81	// GetDatabaseSize returns the database size in bytes, or -1 if unavailable.
82	func (d *DB) GetDatabaseSize(ctx context.Context) (int64, error) {
83		var pageCount, pageSize int64
84		if err := d.db.QueryRowContext(ctx, "PRAGMA page_count").Scan(&pageCount); err != nil {
85			return -1, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read page_count")
86		}
87		if err := d.db.QueryRowContext(ctx, "PRAGMA page_size").Scan(&pageSize); err != nil {
88			return -1, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read page_size")
89		}
90		return pageCount * pageSize, nil
91	}

21	// NewTestingStore creates a new testing store with a fresh database.
22	// Each test gets its own isolated database:
23	//   - SQLite: new temp file per test
24	//   - MySQL/PostgreSQL: new database per test in shared container
25	func NewTestingStore(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T) *store.Store {
26		driver := getDriverFromEnv()
27		profile := getTestingProfileForDriver(t, driver)
28		dbDriver, err := db.NewDBDriver(profile)
29		if err != nil {
30			t.Fatalf("failed to create db driver: %v", err)
31		}

33		store := store.New(dbDriver, profile)

36		}

38	}

40	// NewTestingStoreWithDSN creates a testing store connected to a specific DSN.
41	// This is useful for testing migrations on existing data.
42	func NewTestingStoreWithDSN(_ context.Context, t *testing.T, driver, dsn string) *store.Store {
43		profile := &profile.Profile{
44			Port:    getUnusedPort(),
45			Data:    t.TempDir(), // Dummy dir, DSN matters
46			DSN:     dsn,
47			Driver:  driver,
48			Version: version.GetCurrentVersion(),
49		}
50		dbDriver, err := db.NewDBDriver(profile)
51		if err != nil {
52			t.Fatalf("failed to create db driver: %v", err)
53		}
54	
55		store := store.New(dbDriver, profile)
56		// Do not run Migrate() automatically, as we might be testing pre-migration state
57		// or want to run it manually.
58		return store
59	}

61	func getUnusedPort() int {
62		// Get a random unused port
63		listener, err := net.Listen("tcp", "localhost:0")
64		if err != nil {
65			panic(err)
66		}
67		defer listener.Close()
68	
69		// Get the port number
70		port := listener.Addr().(*net.TCPAddr).Port
71		return port
72	}

76		// Attempt to load .env file if present (optional, for local development)
77		_ = godotenv.Load(".env")
78	
79		// Get a temporary directory for the test data.
80		dir := t.TempDir()
81		mode := "prod"
82		port := getUnusedPort()
83

86		case "sqlite":
87			dsn = fmt.Sprintf("%s/memos_%s.db", dir, mode)
88		case "mysql":
89			dsn = GetMySQLDSN(t)
90		case "postgres":
